name: CME_Reviewer_Checklist
description: Compute-Matched Evaluation (CME) Standards for Multi-Agent and Scaled Inference Submissions
instructions: For each question, select the appropriate response and provide a brief justification (with section or appendix references where applicable). If your paper does not evaluate multi-agent systems or test-time compute, select 'Not Applicable'.

questions.title: Resource Vector R Specification
questions.prompt: Does the submission explicitly report the verification status (Strictly Controlled, Approximately Matched, Unmatched, or Unreported) of the six resource dimensions: thinking tokens (R_reason), total tokens (R_token), monetary cost (R_cost), execution latency (R_lat), sample count (R_sample), and system tool overhead (R_sys)?

explanation_field.title: Justification & Section Reference
explanation_field.description: State where the resource accounting vector is documented in the text (e.g., Section 4, Table 1).

questions.title: Equal-Compute Single-Agent Baselines
questions.prompt: When comparing against a single agent, is the baseline allocated an equivalent compute budget (e.g., self-consistency CoT-SC, Best-of-N, or extended reasoning tokens) rather than solely a single greedy call?

explanation_field.title: Baseline Specification
explanation_field.description: Describe the single-agent baseline used to match compute (e.g., CoT-SC with K=5, budget-matched thinking tokens).

questions.title: Scaffolding and Context Echoing Overhead
questions.prompt: Are system prompts, role headers, echoed message histories, and routing calls deducted from the multi-agent system's effective reasoning budget?

explanation_field.title: Scaffold Accounting Details
explanation_field.description: State how non-reasoning scaffold tokens were measured and accounted for.

questions.title: Sample Rigor and Paired Dispersion Reporting
questions.prompt: Does the submission report benchmark test sizes (N_items) and run-to-run dispersion, with paired statistics or per-instance binary outcomes disclosed?

explanation_field.title: Sample Rigor Details
explanation_field.description: List benchmark sample sizes and dispersion metrics reported (e.g., confidence intervals, paired McNemar p-values).

questions.title: Task Decomposability and Ground-Truth Verifiers
questions.prompt: Does the paper characterize task decomposability and test whether single agents equipped with equivalent external tools (e.g., compilers, unit tests, retrieval engines) achieve identical gains?

explanation_field.title: Tool and Verifier Isolation
explanation_field.description: Explain how communicative coordination is separated from tool access.

questions.title: Full Architecture Search and Negative Results Disclosure
questions.prompt: Are cumulative compute expenditures across exploratory topology searches and negative graph configurations disclosed?

explanation_field.title: Search Budget Disclosure
explanation_field.description: Disclose search tokens/costs and negative results, or indicate that manual fixed topologies were evaluated.

evaluation_rules.pattern: Multi-agent beats greedy single agent, but trails or matches CoT-SC / Best-of-N at equal budget
evaluation_rules.reasoning: Apparent advantage is confounded by ensembling and repeated sampling rather than coordination.

evaluation_rules.pattern: Multi-agent scales tokens or monetary cost by >5x without budget-matched single-agent baselines
evaluation_rules.reasoning: Strawman baseline comparison; gains uncredited to compute scaling.

evaluation_rules.pattern: Multi-agent system outperforms single-agent search under strictly matched thinking tokens or Pareto frontier
evaluation_rules.reasoning: Genuine evidence of architectural or communicative coordination efficiency.

evaluation_rules.pattern: Multi-agent system demonstrates clear Pareto efficiency on tool-partitioned tasks with ground-truth verifiers
evaluation_rules.reasoning: Valid structural deployment with complete resource vector reporting.
